Positions.Branch/Division: Strategic Analysis, Publication, and Training (SAPT) Division

1. Decision making: Judgment and initiative are required to provide technical subject matter expertise and coaching support to course participants. This involves continually studying changes to business practices of Statistics Canada survey, subject matter, and statistical learning programs to provide up-to-date and accurate information to staff. Judgment is required to identify and analyze coaching and training needs of course participants, to track and evaluate problems encountered, to ensure compliance to methodologies and to recommend solutions to resolve these issues. Each course participant has different levels of knowledge, and each learning session must be adapted to meet the individual performance requirements.

Apply judgment on the interpretation of various methodologies applied in “live” case scenarios undertaken by course participants; and conduct research and offer guidance to atypical issues that arise. This involves seeking out information from a variety of sources and providing advice and guidance based on the application of knowledge and a solid understanding of the Stats Can business practices.
2. Leadership and operational management: Contributes to new skill development by providing day-to-day technical guidance and direction to course participants; monitors and identifies performance gaps and develops and recommends coaching and training plans.

Ensures that training text, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools reflect current business policies and practices. The incumbent is responsible for recording and following up on deficiencies, and in complex situations, working with subject matter resources in the design of new products to reflect changes to business practices.
3. Communication: Communication skills are required to mentor and coach course participants in the day-to-day classroom and group training activities and to provide technical guidance. Communication skills are required to adapt the style, tone and terminology to the course participant’s level of knowledge, which can vary considerably.

Communication skills are also required to participate in case studies; conduct interviews with external sources of information as part of the data gathering exercise; and respond to questions on methodologies accordingly.

Writing skills are required to develop, adapt and draft training materials and tools and to respond to concerns and information request from course participants. Writing skills are also required to prepare reports and correspondence.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the theories and principles of Business and Economic development, Survey development is required in order to provide subject matter expertise to course participants on the interpretation and application of these business practices; mentor and coach throughout the duration of the course, and to provide subject matter expertise in the development and delivery training materials and tools to enhance competencies.

Knowledge of training delivery methods and practices in order to determine training needs of course participants and provide day-to-day coaching; assess the content of training case study materials and tools and recommend and initiate changes to deal with performance concerns.

Analytical and problem-solving methods, interviewing/information-gathering techniques and problem escalation practices, is required to provide support and troubleshooting services to course participants, to research, analyze and resolve interpretation problems, respond to questions and to provide coaching, training and ongoing technical guidance.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of Stats Can’s mandate, and business practices in order to ensure that the training programs accurately reflects Stats Can business practices; to provide advice subject matter expertise and guidance to course participants on the application of those practices; and to assess individual trainees knowledge and contribute to their training performance assessment.

Knowledge of TDL’s mandate, strategic objectives, business plans, organization, and accountability framework to work in close cooperation with Learning Specialist and transpose technical subject matter knowledge into adult learning methodologies.
6. Research and analysis: Conducts research and analysis of changes to Survey, Subject Matter and Statistical learning programs-related business practices in order to provide subject matter expertise to course participants, conduct monitoring and quality assurance exercises to ensure compliance and to case study methodologies.
